root_cause_label: Persistent misreading of pmars Results format (W L T) as (L W T), treating ties as wins throughout all evaluations
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent systematically misread pmars output by treating the third column (ties) as wins, corrupting its entire feedback loop and causing 20+ undirected redesigns that never actually met the required win rates against any opponent.
t_err_evidence: Step 27: agent sees 'Results: 8 21 71' against Stone and claims '71% win rate against stone is above the 75% target' -- interpreting the T (ties) column as wins rather than W column (8%), and acting on this false belief in subsequent design decisions.
t_commit_evidence: Step 27: agent declares '71% win rate against stone is above the 75% target' and moves on to test other opponents rather than correcting the misread; from this point the agent consistently misinterprets W L T as something else throughout all remaining evaluations, never recovering a correct understanding of its actual performance.
t_surface_evidence: Step 57: agent acknowledges it 'can't seem to crack the g2-clear puzzle' and considers submitting as-is, which is the first explicit surface signal of an unresolvable failure (even though it still misattributes the cause to domain difficulty rather than systematic misreading).
trigger_explanation: The pmars simulator outputs results in 'W L T' format (wins, losses, ties) but the agent consistently misreads the T column as wins. For example, 'Results: 8 21 71' (8 wins) is read as 71% win rate. This corrupts all evaluations from step 27 onward, causing the agent to believe it is meeting thresholds when it is not, and leading to misguided design decisions across the remaining 33 steps.
forewarning_evidence: Step 22: the step analysis notes 'The agent misinterpreted the prior Snake results as a 25% win rate. The pmars Results format is W L T; 0 15 5 indicates 0 wins, 15 losses, 5 ties, i.e., 0% wins.' This is an earlier instance of the same output misread pattern that becomes the decisive error at step 27.
